paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: the Lord stays with you when the work gets hard. Paul got opposed and insulted in Corinth, and then the Lord spoke to him in a vision: "Do not be afraid; keep on speaking; do not be silent." (Acts 18:9) That's not a pep talk from a stranger. The Lord gives a reason: "For I am with you and no one will lay a hand on you, because I have many people in this city." (Acts 18:10)

Now notice what that means for you. The Lord doesn't only say "keep going." He tells Paul who is already in that city, people Paul hasn't even met yet, and Crispus and many Corinthians believed (Acts 18:8). So when a door shuts, like it did in the synagogue (Acts 18:6), the work isn't over. I spent years in the back of a junk drawer thinking my story was done, and the Lord had a whole bakery waiting. Closed door, open house next door. I'm not saying it's always that fast, but the Lord is always already ahead of you!

And look at how Paul's year and a half in Corinth (Acts 18:11) ended up. Paul never got to speak at the judgment seat, and still Gallio drove the accusers away (Acts 18:14-16). Paul's job was to keep speaking, and the Lord handled what he couldn't. So keep showing up to the Word, baker, even when you feel worn down at the edges like I was. You're not baking alone, and the Lord has more people in your city than you know. The story isn't over, either, and there's more of Paul's journey still ahead.
